chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Saeed, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abdul A'ala, the slave of the progeny of Saam, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'How much was the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It was three thousand and six hundred cubits, broken (squared).'

key_terms.مَسْجِدُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The Mosque of the Messenger of Allah
key_terms.مُكَسَّراً: Broken/Squared (referring to the shape or measurement style)

ai.seo_question: What were the dimensions of the Prophet's Mosque during the time of the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi provides precise historical data on the original footprint of Masjid al-Nabi, with the term 'mukassaran' indicating a calculated or squared measurement of the enclosed area. It serves as a foundational reference for understanding the architectural evolution of the Prophet's Mosque from its modest beginnings to its expanded forms under subsequent caliphs. The narration highlights the scholarly tradition of preserving specific physical details of sacred sites to maintain historical accuracy.
